I've set up the Light Cycles project in `.planning/` (`PROJECT.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `STATE.md`) and added it to the cross-project portfolio. Every requirement and decision comes from `TASK.md` and `docs/spec.md`. The project is in autonomous mode, so I didn't ask any questions and took the default at each confirmation step, including accepting the phase list below as drafted. There's no code in the repo yet, so I skipped mapping it.

| # | Phase | Requirements | Plans (est.) | Personas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Engine and test hook:** game-rules code with no browser dependencies, the `window.tron` hook, and `node --test` tests | REQ-03–06, 11, 12 | 2 | senior-developer, qa-verification-specialist |
| 2 | **Playable game:** canvas drawing, keyboard controls, 15 ticks per second, start/pause/round/match flow, colours | REQ-01, 02, 07–09 | 2 | frontend-developer, ui-designer, qa-verification-specialist |
| 3 | **Computer player:** `chooseMove`, tested against bots of increasing strength on obstacle arenas as either player, under 20 ms | REQ-10 | 3 | ai-engineer, senior-developer, performance-benchmarker |

There are 12 requirements, REQ-01 to REQ-12. Out of scope: two human players or online play, build tools or dependencies, obstacles in normal play, and touch controls.

Main design decision: the rules and the computer player are plain JavaScript modules that don't touch the page, so the browser game and `node --test` use the same code. The computer player gets its own phase because its strength is scored and will need repeated tuning against the test bots.

Nothing is committed yet; that's your call.
